message:
feat(update): ask from the tray, and never call a failed check "up to date"

The check has five answers, not two. NotConfigured, Unreachable, Rejected,
UpToDate, UpdateAvailable. Collapsing those into a boolean is how a machine
that has failed to reach its update server for a month ends up telling its user
it is current, and that is the failure this enum exists to prevent.

NotConfigured is answered before any socket is opened. A build with no trusted
key cannot accept a manifest whatever the server says, so fetching one would be
theatre -- and the error it produced would read as "the update server is
broken" rather than "this build does not do updates yet".

Nothing blocks the caller. The synchronous form is a plain function a test can
call; the asynchronous form runs detached and hands the answer to a callback.
That the callback arrives on the worker thread is stated in the header rather
than glossed over, because glossing over it is how a worker ends up touching
windows it does not own -- so the tray posts a message and the UI thread shows
the box.

The menu item stays enabled when signed out. Whether a newer build exists has
nothing to do with being signed in, and greying it out would make an
unconfigured build look like a broken one.

Two test defects found in review are fixed here too. "Nothing leaks in the
body" was satisfied by there being no body at all, so it passed hardest exactly
when the server was unreachable; it now requires a response first. And running
the route test alone produced fifteen confusing failures instead of saying it
needs the server the suite starts.

Not verified: nobody has clicked the menu item. Running the freshly built host
would collide with the live one on this machine, so the wiring is covered by a
build and unit tests only. With no key and no URL configured it currently
answers NotConfigured every time, which is the honest answer.

qwinsta: console active, rdp-tcp listening. 28 checks here; 444 across the
seven update suites. The three live PIDs are unchanged.
